audit_findings.title: Redeemable NCI is an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $311 million latest filed claim, equal to $0.76 per diluted share and 2.2% of $14.291 billion base equity value; deduction lowers the base value to about $34.31 per share and the 30% MOS threshold to about $24.02 versus the $21.97 price
audit_findings.mechanism: The redeemable NCI must be deducted in the common-equity bridge because consolidated operating cash flows include Altosano while its outside owners hold a fair-value redemption claim.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 28, 2025, the value of the NCI on our consolidated balance sheet was $264 million.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge omission, and the audit's $264 million evidence is superseded by the June 2026 filed value of $311 million. The correction reduces value, but by itself does not change the conclusion that the market price is below the base-case buy-below threshold.
audit_findings.action: Rerun every scenario with a $311 million NCI deduction, or a later filed redemption value if available, while retaining the deduction of NCI earnings from OE.

audit_findings.title: Nathan's creates a cross-date perimeter mismatch
audit_findings.magnitude: $450 million to $500 million expected consideration; net valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The transaction affects the cash/debt bridge and, after closing, the operating perimeter and OE through acquired earnings, assumed debt, transaction costs, and elimination of existing royalties.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to pay approximately $450 to $500 million for our pending acquisition of Nathan’s, including transaction costs and the payoff of assumed debt.
audit_findings.explanation: The June 2026 filing establishes that Nathan's had not closed by June 28 and remained contingent, so the bridge contains pre-acquisition cash and debt while the valuation date is later. Reserving the entire consideration without recognizing the acquired business would lower the base MOS threshold by about $0.77 to $0.86 per share, which alone would not reverse the conclusion, but the record does not establish the transaction's September 5 status or the value of acquired earnings and royalty savings.
audit_findings.action: Establish whether the acquisition closed by September 5, 2026; then rerun using one date-consistent perimeter containing the actual consideration, assumed debt, transaction costs, post-close cash, acquired OE, and discontinued royalty payments.

audit_findings.title: Latest-year OE may capitalize a cyclical high
audit_findings.magnitude: OE increased $263.1 million, or 40.9%, from $643.1 million in 2024 to $906.2 million in 2025; Hog Production operating profit swung $320 million from a $144 million loss to a $176 million profit; an approximately $106.8 million, or 11.8%, anchor reduction would erase the base-case MOS threshold buffer
audit_findings.mechanism: The $906.2 million latest-year OE is the DCF anchor, so any above-cycle earnings are capitalized through explicit-period growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: We operate in a cyclical industry and our results are significantly affected by fluctuations in commodity prices for meat, livestock (primarily hogs) and grains.
audit_findings.explanation: A peak-year error is not demonstrated, but materiality is. The filed cyclicality, the large Hog Production reversal, and the 40.9% OE increase are substantially larger than the approximately 11.8% anchor reduction required to move the base buy-below threshold down to the market price. The too-hard flag describes the uncertainty but does not reduce its valuation effect.
audit_findings.action: Build a filed-data normalization across a complete hog and feed-price cycle, reconcile segment margins and hedging effects, and rerun all scenarios with the resulting mid-cycle OE anchor.

audit_findings.title: Large replacement-plant spending may be missing from OE
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to $1.3 billion proposed over three years; $37 million land purchase closed after quarter-end; replacement or maintenance portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any continuity or replacement component belongs in maintenance capital expenditure and reduces OE; project spending and closure costs also affect the cash bridge during construction.
audit_findings.evidence: Our preliminary estimate of the proposed investment is up to $1.3 billion over the next three years.
audit_findings.explanation: The project would replace an operating 117-year-old plant, making a maintenance component plausible, but the June 2026 filing still describes construction as contingent on board and regulatory approvals. The total proposal cannot be treated as maintenance capital without an allocation, so it is a forward-looking item to monitor rather than a presently demonstrated OE error.
audit_findings.action: Monitor board approval, permitting, construction commitments, and updated cost guidance; once committed, separate continuity capacity from expansion and efficiency spending and rerun OE with the recurring economic replacement cost or explicit project cash flows.

audit_findings.title: Underfunded pensions may remain ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $194 million filed FY2025 funded-status deficit and $27 million expected 2026 contributions; funding after 2026 unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash contributions exceeding pension expense reduce OE, while any unfunded obligation not captured by projected OE may require a common-equity bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, the Company’s defined benefit pension obligation was $1.82 billion, offset by the fair value of plan assets totaling $1.62 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: The funded deficit is demonstrated, but a valuation error is not: pension expense is already within earnings, and the record does not show whether OE adjustments capture contribution timing. The $194 million deficit alone is about 1.4% of base equity value and would lower the base MOS threshold by about $0.33 per share, insufficient to change the conclusion. Materiality remains unresolved because the filing cannot reliably estimate contribution timing beyond 2026 and the deficit is assumption-sensitive.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile pension expense, OE adjustments, qualified and non-qualified cash contributions, plan assets, and benefit payments; obtain the latest funded-status roll-forward and rerun only for cash funding not already captured in OE.

audit_findings.title: Equity-method value may be counted twice
audit_findings.magnitude: $12 million FY2025 equity-method income and $209 million stake addition; if the full $12 million remained in OE, its base-case capitalized value is approximately $168.6 million, or $0.41 per share, lowering the MOS threshold by about $0.29 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Affiliate income must be removed from the OE anchor when the associated investments are valued separately in the equity bridge; the bridge addition must also reflect an appropriate stake value net of associated commitments.
audit_findings.evidence: We record our share of earnings and losses from our equity method investments in (income) loss from equity method investments in the consolidated statements of income.
audit_findings.explanation: Double counting is possible but not demonstrated because the supplied OE reconciliation does not show whether the $12 million was removed. Even complete retention of that income would overstate base equity by about 1.2% and would not change the price-versus-buy-below conclusion. The separate $209 million carrying-value addition is only 1.5% of base equity value, although its valuation basis still requires verification.
